title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being acted on as though it were a confirmed identification. A camera system flagged a stolen Camaro, an undercover unit saw a car that appeared to match, and the stop escalated to at least five patrol cars, a helicopter, drawn guns and handcuffs. The failure sits at the handoff between the system's flag and the officers who had to act on it: deputies and the helicopter crew could not read the plates, so the match was never verified before force was used.

Catching it would have required the one step that was missing, confirming the plate on the car in front of them before treating the occupants as armed robbery suspects. The system produced a lead, and a lead is not an identification. A rule requiring plate confirmation, or a supervisor's sign off, before a stop of that scale would have interrupted the sequence at the point where the error entered.

What is not established is whether department procedures were followed, which the sheriff's office says supervisors will review using body worn camera footage. The account of the threat to shoot and the push comes from one of the men, and no finding has been made. Both men plan to file complaints, and a complaint is not a determination.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in a Cypress neighborhood, Harris County sheriff's deputies stopped two 19 year old men, Anthony and Julian, after mistaking their Camaro for a stolen car. Flock cameras had flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. An undercover unit saw a matching car, but deputies and a helicopter could not read its plates, so backup was called. At least five patrol cars and a helicopter arrived. Deputies pointed guns, handcuffed the men, and Julian said a deputy pushed him down and threatened to shoot him. He had cuts and scrapes.

Deputies soon realized it was the wrong car and that the men were not suspects. Anthony's mother wants accountability and plans to hire an attorney. The sheriff's office says supervisors, including the district captain and shift lieutenants and sergeants, will review body worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed. The men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
